1.pericope_label: Rejoice in the LORD, O ye righteous: for praise is comely for the upright

sides.view: Eight manuscripts join it to the preceding psalm, and its first verse may once have closed that one
A separate anonymous congregational song that merely opens as the previous one closes
The authorship cannot be settled — David, or whoever wrote it

debates.q: What are the instruments of the second verse?

sides.view: A three-cornered harp, and one ten-stringed psaltery rather than two instruments
Instruments used in the public worship of the tabernacle
Childish things given to Israel at school to help her learn
The ten strings are the commandments, three and seven, and the body is the offering

outliers.view: Reads the ten-stringed psaltery as the Decalogue, three commandments and seven, played by members made servants to love
Complains that few singers can adapt sound to sense — they can make a loud noise, but not suit the style of the music to the words

4.pericope_label: For the word of the LORD is right; and all his works are done in truth

debates.q: What is the word by which the heavens were made?

sides.view: The essential Word, who spoke on the six days of creation
The Word with the Spirit — the three persons unite in creating
The breath of his mouth is only a synonym for word; it means his commanding omnipotence
One single word, with neither pains nor time

debates.q: Are the waters gathered as a heap or into a bottle?

sides.view: A heap, the image explaining itself without reference to the Red Sea; the bottle is the ancient reading, recorded not adopted
A heap in the harvest sense, the sea held together above the level of the continents
A standing miracle of physics, the tides bounded by adjusted solar and lunar influence

outliers.view: Reads the bounding of the sea as a problem in celestial mechanics, saying the one economy contains a whole circle of science and needs the nicest of Newtonian calculations

10.pericope_label: The LORD bringeth the counsel of the heathen to nought

debates.q: What is the counsel of the Lord that stands for ever?

sides.view: The eternal decrees — election, redemption, effectual calling, glorification
A list of things already accomplished, down to the Gospel nearly overrunning the earth
His purposes, which are always successful, and which govern even the faculties by which men govern themselves
The Jews, elected and then reprobated for unbelief, with the Gentiles elected in their place
Israel principally, but not exclusively — the chosen people are drawn from Jews and Gentiles alike

outliers.view: States flatly that the Jews were preserved as the heritage for two thousand years and have been reprobated, the Gentiles elected in their place

13.pericope_label: The LORD looketh from heaven; he beholdeth all the sons of men

debates.q: What does it mean that he fashioneth their hearts alike?

sides.view: All hearts are alike as made; later differences come from body, education and circumstance
The same powers, faculties and passions in every human being
Not the making but the subjection — all alike under his government
Redivide the lines: he moulds their hearts for all, as a potter moulds clay

debates.q: Is the horse vain for safety or for victory?

sides.view: For victory — the allusion is to the war-horse, and the king does not triumph by the greatness of his force
For safety, the horse standing for every kind of military preparation that lies when trusted
For escape — a lion or a tiger can overtake him, or he may stumble and kill his rider

outliers.view: Turns the verse into a claim about the origin of the soul, that souls are created and not generated

18.pericope_label: Behold, the eye of the LORD is upon them that fear him

debates.q: From what death are they delivered?

sides.view: Not the bodily one — the godly die as other men; the spiritual and the eternal death are meant
The bodily one — preservation from accident and from lingering death by extraordinary supplies
Safety of any kind, expected only from the watchful eye and almighty hand

debates.q: What is the waiting of the twentieth verse?

sides.view: The church waiting for the coming in the flesh, or for a gracious presence after absence
A whole manner of life that refuses to trust armies, strength or swift animals
Quiet expectation and patient hope, one of the bright attainments of a Christian

outliers.view: Counts the three possessives in the verse and rests the whole matter on them — personal possession makes the Christian man, all else is mere talk
